components.text: The likelihood comparison changes when consciousness and the resources for adventuresome life are included in the evidence.
Specific forms and distributions of suffering may reverse the broad comparison.
The explicit possibility of reversal preserves evidential sensitivity to richer observations.
Compare suffering under theism and indifference while fixing whether consciousness and relevant background knowledge are already given.
Address whether specific severe and unequal suffering reverses any general likelihood advantage for theism.
State conditions under which suffering can count against rather than always favor theism.
